draft.title: The fossil record
card: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of past organisms. Together they form the fossil record, which shows how life has changed over time.
fossils appear in the rock layers in a regular order. Different groups of organisms are found in different layers, and the same order is seen in many places.
fossils of species that were widespread and lived for a short time. Finding one in a rock layer shows the layer formed in that short period.
fossils with features of two groups, such as a fish-like animal with limb bones. They show how one group could give rise to another.
draft.remember: The fossil record shows change over time: order of layers, fossils that mark a period, and fossils that link groups.

a.q: A fossil has features of both an older group and a younger group of animals. What is it called?
a.why: A fossil that combines features of two groups is transitional, as it shows a link between them. An index fossil is tempting, but it is used to match the age of rock layers, not to show links between groups.
a.clue: Think about a fossil that sits between two groups.

b.q: Geologists in Queensland find the same short-lived marine species in rock at two distant sites. What can they conclude?
opts: The two rock layers formed in the same period
The two sites had the same climate throughout
The species gave rise to all later marine animals
The species was rare and lived in one small area
b.why: An index fossil lived for a short time and was widespread, so finding it in two layers suggests they formed in the same period. It does not show the climate or that the species was ancestral, and a rare local species would not work as an index fossil.
b.clue: Which features make a fossil useful for matching layers?

b.best: The two rock layers formed in the same period
